subject: P-values of latent variable loadings summary() vs standardizedSolution()

messages.author: 9cd2f7a3e99756cd
messages.subject: P-values of latent variable loadings summary() vs standardizedSolution()
parts:
Dear all,

I am new to lavaan, just developed a model with an acceptable fit and I am currently trying to interpret the output. What I noticed is that the p-values of the indicators of the latent variables are different in the summary() output vs the standardizedSolution().

I used :
summary(fit_sem, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE), which shows all the loadings <.05 and the std estimates are the ones that appear on the path (under the column std all). 

When I tried: standardizedsolution(fit_sem), under est std the coefficients were the same, the p-values though were much higher. Similarly, the covariances' and regressions' p-values are higher.

Any ideas why is this happening? I suspect there is something to do with the initial latent variable scaling but then why there is the same issue with the covariances ?

Many thanks in advance

Andy

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: P-values of latent variable loadings summary() vs standardizedSolution()
parts: I noticed is that the p-values of the indicators of the latent variables are different in the summary() output vs the standardizedSolution().

See class?summary for a description of that output.  The p values are for the unstandardized parameters, it will only print the standardized estimates on request.  The latter's p values are only available from standardizedSolution()
